statements.text: Trump announced a reciprocal energy ceasefire. Zelenskyy has assured the Prime Minister that Ukraine would implement it immediately once a start date is confirmed, and the Prime Minister will discuss this further with him in the coming days.

A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly shown it is serious about peace, while Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires and continued attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy. The Prime Minister said Russian strikes have intensified further in the three weeks since the New York meeting, with more attacks on civilians, apartment blocks and buses carrying children.

The UK has announced new funding to help Ukraine through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that brings over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity under UK sanctions.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military aid and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks. He is set to tell President Zelenskyy that the UK will accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

Britain has sent air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling, which the government says is needed to protect civilians. The Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. The UK condemns the attacks on King Khalid International Airport and will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

The UK assesses that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The government will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran's and the IRGC's capacity to harm the UK.

The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles to Ukraine and standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports. It will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which the government says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the £45 million package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter needs.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey urged partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, as the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin. He is to urge partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban.

The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for the battlefield in Ukraine, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners, and would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy to Downing Street. The leaders reflected on Russia's attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure since President Trump called for an energy ceasefire, and underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. They discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support to Ukraine ahead of the winter.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration. The government says a food and drink deal would add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, and is expected to lift burdens of up to £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers.

The Prime Minister will invite the First Minister to work with him, through No10 North and the Scotland Office, to develop a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland. Andy Burnham said: 'This is me making an offer to the Scottish Government.' Douglas Alexander said the offer is a genuine one and that the Scotland Office is ready to roll up its sleeves alongside the Scottish Government.

In Motherwell, the Prime Minister offered Scotland a model of localised employment support similar to England's, shaped by Holyrood. He said the National Economic Council will meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, the first such meeting since he became Prime Minister, to put the offer on the table.
The Scottish Government has agreed this week to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west of Scotland.

Chancellor Merz and the Prime Minister agreed a new partnership in Berlin to tackle Russian hybrid threats. The Prime Minister confirmed the commitment to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence, as recommended by the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

The site of Great British Railways' headquarters has been unveiled at Becketwell in Derby. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, and the government estimates the HQ will bring hundreds of rail jobs and a £151 million boost to Derby. Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship.
Heidi Alexander said she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home, bringing jobs, investment and opportunity to Derby.
Pat McFadden said the foundation apprenticeship is part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
